summary: A neighborhood story about Maria Thompson, a 52-year-old graphic designer, adjusting to an empty nest after her youngest child left for college on September 15th, 2023. She and her husband David build new routines, revive date nights, return to art and music, and make new social connections while keeping close to their children through weekly video calls. The story frames the transition as a mix of nostalgia and renewed potential.
one_line: After her youngest left for college in September 2023, Maria Thompson adapts to an empty nest by rebuilding routines, partnership, passions and community.
key_facts: Maria Thompson waved goodbye to her youngest child, who left for college, on September 15th, 2023.
Maria Thompson is a 52-year-old graphic designer who works from a home office; her husband David is 55 and an accountant.
The Thompsons raised two children, Chloe and Alex, over more than two decades.
On September 20th, 2023, Maria began taking morning walks in the nearby park.
Maria told her friend Susan by phone around September 23rd that she finally had time to try recipes she had been pinning for years.
Maria and David started a weekly-style "date night" on September 25th at a small Italian restaurant downtown, having let the concept lapse amid soccer practices and ballet recitals.
On October 12th, 2023, Maria dedicated a room solely to her art, dusting off her sketchbooks and easels.
David picked up his guitar again after setting music aside for family responsibilities.
Maria attended a local book club meeting on October 15th, where she met fellow empty nesters.
Maria joined a community garden initiative on October 22nd.
Maria, Chloe and Alex hold weekly video calls; on November 1st Maria said "there's warmth in knowing we've raised you to spread your wings and fly."
Maria realized "It's okay to miss them and still enjoy this new chapter."
